title: Chevron Earnings Beat Estimates as Refining Surge Lifts Profit to $9.9 Billion on $67.8 Billion Revenue
excerpt: Adjusted EPS of $5.28 beat the $4.78 consensus as downstream earnings quadrupled on record refinery throughput, free cash flow hit $12 billion and debt fell again.
body:
• Chevron's third-quarter earnings nearly tripled to $9.9 billion, or $5.06 per share; adjusted earnings of $10.4 billion, or $5.28 per share, beat the $4.78 Zacks consensus by 10.5%.
  • Revenue jumped 36.3% to $67.8 billion, well above the $60.5 billion consensus, as downstream earnings climbed to $4.9 billion on record U.S. refinery throughput of 1.09 million barrels per day at 98% utilization.
  • Upstream earnings rose 72.6% to $5.7 billion on stronger realizations even as worldwide production slipped 2.6% to 3,980 MBOE/d; U.S. production topped 2 million barrels per day for a fifth straight quarter.
  • Free cash flow surged to $12 billion, total debt fell to $33.5 billion, and the board declared a $1.78 quarterly dividend payable December 10.

Chevron Corporation reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $9.9 billion, or $5.06 per diluted share, the company announced Friday in its official results release, up from $3.5 billion a year earlier as refining margins and stronger crude realizations overwhelmed a modest decline in production. Adjusted earnings were $10.4 billion, or $5.28 per diluted share, after items including a $160 million legal reserve, a $110 million impairment and $143 million of unfavorable foreign-currency effects.

Both engines beat

The adjusted $5.28 per share beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.78 by 10.5% and surged 185% from $1.85 a year ago, while revenue of $67.8 billion rose 36.3% year over year and topped the $60.5 billion consensus by 12.1%. Upstream earnings rose 72.6% to $5.7 billion: U.S. production averaged 2,043 MBOE/d, held up by ramp-ups at Ballymore, Whale and Anchor in the Gulf of America, and U.S. upstream earnings climbed to $3.3 billion as domestic liquids realizations rose 30% to $62.72 per barrel. International production fell 5.3% to 1,937 MBOE/d, but higher realizations still lifted overseas upstream earnings 19% to $2.4 billion.

Downstream was the bigger swing. Earnings climbed to $4.9 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, with U.S. downstream contributing $3.6 billion as refinery crude inputs rose to a record 1,093 thousand barrels per day at nearly 98% utilization. International downstream earnings rose to $1.3 billion despite refined-product sales falling 8.5% on supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict, which also weighed on worldwide production volumes.

“We delivered strong operational performance and disciplined execution, while continuing to invest to grow energy supply.”

— Mike Wirth, Chairman and CEO, Chevron

Cash, debt and Venezuela

Operating cash flow reached $16.0 billion, up from $9.4 billion a year earlier, and free cash flow surged to $12 billion from $4.9 billion as capital spending fell 9.7% to $4 billion. Chevron returned $3.5 billion in dividends and about $2.5 billion in buybacks during the quarter, ended September with $12.8 billion of cash, and cut total debt to $33.5 billion from $40.8 billion at the end of 2025, taking its net debt ratio down to 9.6%. The board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share, payable December 10, 2026, to holders of record on November 18.

Growth plans leaned heavily on Venezuela, where Chevron secured improved commercial terms and additional acreage; its joint ventures intend to invest about $7 billion over five years and more than double production, from roughly 280,000 barrels per day toward 600,000 by 2031. The company also announced agreements targeting about 50% lower Bakken midstream costs, a new discovery in Angola and exploration agreements covering Libya.
